# A polynomial certificate for frozen encoded variables during a transverse-field hold

Status: independently derived theorem and reproducible small-matrix checks for
this trial. This is a conditional, closed-system, finite-time result. It is not a
claim about the success of a complete forward anneal or a real noisy processor.

Research subtask started 2026-10-07 at approximately 20:11 UTC. The first recorded
clock read was 20:12:01 UTC. The inherited trial deadline is 21:55:30 UTC. Only the
lab's `prompt.md` and public sources were read; no prior lab or author guidance was
used. Scientific-trial child session ID:
`01a117fe-0bfd-7be3-bceb-77efccafaa8b`.

## Model and inexpensive inputs

Fix a valid minor embedding with disjoint connected branch sets
\(C_1,\ldots,C_L\), using \(N=\sum_i |C_i|\) physical qubits. At a fixed
anneal coordinate, hold the transverse-field Hamiltonian constant for time \(t\):

\[
 H=C+D-\Gamma\sum_{q=1}^N X_q,\qquad
 C=\sum_{qr\in E_{\rm chain}} c_{qr}(1-Z_qZ_r),\quad c_{qr}>0.
\]

Here \(D\) contains all programmed problem fields and inter-branch couplings and
is diagonal in the computational basis. Constants are discarded. Use
\(\hbar=1\), so time is measured in reciprocal units of Hamiltonian energy.
This is exactly the prompt's Hamiltonian up to a scalar offset when

\[
 \Gamma=A(u_*)/2,\quad c_{qr}=B(u_*)|J^{\rm chain}_{qr}|/2,\quad
 D={B(u_*)\over2}\left(\sum_qh_qZ_q+
             \sum_{qr\in E_{\rm problem}}J_{qr}Z_qZ_r\right).
\]

The programmed coefficients in these equations already include *every*
hardware rescaling factor. A large unscaled chain penalty does not imply an
arbitrarily large physical \(c\) under a finite coupling range.

Let \(P\) project onto states in which every branch set is constant and set
\(Q=I-P\). Its rank is \(2^L\); it includes all encoded assignments, not just
the optimum. For each nonsingleton branch, compute its minimum positive weighted
cut \(\kappa_i=\min_{\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq C_i}
\sum_{qr\in\partial S}c_{qr}\). Define

\[
 \Delta=2\min_{i:|C_i|>1}\kappa_i,\qquad
 R=\sum_q|d_q|+\sum_{qr}|d_{qr}|\ \geq\ \|D\|.
\]

Then \(C P=0\) and \(QCQ\succeq\Delta Q\). Write \(n_1\) for the number
of singleton branches, \(n_2\) for the number of branches of size two, and
\(M=N-n_1\), the number of physical qubits in nonsingleton branches. Define

\[
 g=\Delta-2R-\Gamma(N+n_1),\qquad
 b=\Gamma\sqrt{M+2n_2}.
\]

The evaluator requires \(g>0\); otherwise it returns **inconclusive**, not a
claim that the embedding has bad dynamics. With no nonsingleton branches,
\(P=I\) and there is no approximation error. With \(\Gamma=0\), all encoded
computational-basis probabilities are exactly frozen without needing \(g>0\).

## Finite-time theorem

If \(g>0\), set \(s=b/g\). For every \(t\geq0\),

\[
 \left\|\left(e^{-itH}-e^{-itPHP}\right)P\right\|
 \leq \varepsilon(t)
 :=2s+t\,{b^2\over g}\exp(2s).
 \tag{1}
\]

The exponential of \(PHP\) on the right is restricted to \(P\). This estimate
holds uniformly for *every* initial pure state in \(P\), and by purification
for every density matrix \(\rho=P\rho P\). It does not assume a unique
logical or physical ground state. One may cap an operator-norm bound at two and
a probability bound at one.

On the encoded space the first-order Hamiltonian is exactly

\[
 PHP=D_{\rm logical}-\Gamma\sum_{i:|C_i|=1}X_i^{\rm logical}.
 \tag{2}
\]

Consequently, if \(F\) is any physical measurement effect whose restriction to
\(P\) is a diagonal event depending only on nonsingleton logical variables,
then for every such initial state

\[
 |\operatorname{Tr}(F e^{-itH}\rho e^{itH})-
            \operatorname{Tr}(F\rho)|\leq\min(1,\varepsilon(t)).
 \tag{3}
\]

The definition of \(F\) on broken-chain states can be arbitrary. Thus the
bound applies both to strict consistent-ground-state success and to any fixed
chain recovery rule agreeing on consistent states. If every branch is a
nonsingleton, \(F\) may be the projector onto *all* optimal decoding assignments,
including any degeneracy. Starting outside that set, the stronger bound
\(p_{\rm repair}(t)\leq\min(1,\varepsilon(t)^2)\) holds. More generally this
square bound applies to every such event with zero initial probability. Leakage
itself has probability at most \(\min(1,\varepsilon(t)^2)\).

This provides a substantive negative certificate: very robust chains can make
a hold incapable of appreciable logical correction. Conversely, for a state
whose encoded values should remain fixed it is a retention certificate. A
smaller bound alone is not an ordering of full annealing success.

## Proof, with explicit constants

Put \(A=PHP\), \(F_Q=QHQ\), and
\(H_0=A\oplus F_Q\). Write \(V=H-H_0\); this is purely block off diagonal.
First,

\[
 \lambda_{\max}(A)\leq R+\Gamma n_1,\qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(F_Q)\geq\Delta-R-\Gamma N.
\]

Their ordered spectral separation is therefore at least \(g\). These coarse
bounds use only coefficient norms, not exponentially costly diagonalization.

Second, the exact off-diagonal norm is \(\|V\|=b\). To see this, set
\(B=QHP\). A physical \(X_q\) on a singleton never leaves \(P\); every
\(X_q\) on a nonsingleton does. In
\(B^\dagger B=\Gamma^2\sum_{q,r}P X_qQX_rP\), an encoded state can return
to \(P\) after two flips only when \(q=r\) or when \(q,r\) are the two
vertices of a size-two branch. Hence

\[
 B^\dagger B=\Gamma^2\left(MP+2\sum_{i:|C_i|=2}X_i^{\rm logical}\right).
\]

The logical \(X_i\)'s commute and have a simultaneous all-positive eigenstate,
giving \(\|B\|=\|V\|=\Gamma\sqrt{M+2n_2}\). This calculation does not
make an assumption about the allocation of the diagonal coefficients.

Choose \(a=R+\Gamma n_1\). The Sylvester equation

\[
 F_QY-YA=B
\]

has the solution
\(Y=\int_0^\infty e^{-(F_Q-a)r}B e^{(A-a)r}\,dr\), with
\(\|Y\|\leq b/g\). Define the anti-Hermitian operator

\[
 S=\begin{pmatrix}0&-Y^\dagger\\Y&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \|S\|=\|Y\|\leq s.
\]

Then \([S,H_0]=-V\). The convergent finite-dimensional conjugation expansion
has an exact first-order cancellation:

\[
 e^SHe^{-S}=H_0+E,\qquad
 E=\sum_{k=1}^\infty {k\over(k+1)!}\operatorname{ad}_S^k(V).
\]

Since \(\|\operatorname{ad}_S^k(V)\|\leq(2s)^k b\) and
\(k/(k+1)!\leq1/[2(k-1)!]\),

\[
 \|E\|\leq bs e^{2s}={b^2\over g}e^{2s}.
\]

The unitary \(e^S\) satisfies \(\|e^S-I\|\leq\|S\|\). Duhamel's
formula bounds the difference between the evolutions of \(H_0+E\) and
\(H_0\) by \(t\|E\|\). The two conjugating unitaries contribute at most
\(2\|S\|\), proving (1). Equation (2) follows by projecting individual
physical flips. In the ideal evolution all events described in (3) commute
with \(A\), so their probabilities are constant. The trace distance of pure
states is at most their vector-norm distance, and purification gives the same
measurement bound for mixed states. Projection onto \(Q\) gives the leakage
bound. If an event has zero initial probability, its positive square root
annihilates the ideal evolved state. Applying that contraction to the vector
difference gives the stronger squared bound. No adiabatic theorem or
nondegenerate perturbation formula is used.

For multiple piecewise constant holds with the same embedding, one can telescope
the operator bounds against the ideal projected evolution to obtain a sum of
the individual \(\varepsilon_j\). Each ideal intermediate state remains in
\(P\). This is mathematically valid but can be loose; it does not cover a
continuous schedule without an independently controlled discretization error.

A limited extension admits initial broken-chain probability
\(\eta=\operatorname{Tr}(Q\rho)\). For a computational-basis event with zero
initial probability, and whose restriction to \(P\) is frozen as above,
\(p(t)\leq\min[1,(\varepsilon(t)\sqrt{1-\eta}+\sqrt\eta)^2]\).
Decompose a purification into its orthogonal \(P\) and \(Q\) components;
the event annihilates the ideal evolution of the former, while unitary
evolution preserves the latter's norm. The triangle inequality proves the
claim. Thus a certified or independently estimated initial leakage bound can
be incorporated, although this work does not infer that bound from a previous
uncontrolled annealing segment.

## Computational cost and selection rule

Given the embedding and coefficient allocation, \(R,N,n_1,n_2,M\) take
\(O(N+|E|)\) time and linear input memory. For tree branches, the minimum cut
is the minimum edge weight, so the entire evaluator is linear in programmed
model size. For arbitrary positive-weight connected branches, a global weighted
min-cut algorithm gives a polynomial certificate; a simple dense Stoer-Wagner
implementation costs \(O(\sum_i|C_i|^3)\) time and
\(O(\max_i|C_i|^2+N+|E|)\) memory. Alternatively, twice the minimum positive
edge weight in a selected spanning tree is a valid inexpensive lower bound on
\(\Delta\). Replacing \(\Delta\) by a lower bound preserves the theorem.

The public function `pause_certificate` in `scripts/theory_checks.py` uses the
linear tree routine or NetworkX weighted min-cut. It returns parameters,
conditions, and bounds separately. No eigenvalue problem occurs in evaluation.
The exponential matrices in that file are validation only and scale as
\(O(2^{3N})\) time and \(O(2^{2N})\) memory.

For a proposed pause intended to repair an encoded variable, reject a candidate
if its certified success upper bound lies below an independently established
success lower bound for another candidate. If the gap condition fails, or
the intervals overlap, report an inconclusive comparison. The construction
algorithm need not alter its general sparse-matrix input interface to use this
certificate; only the theorem's useful regime is restricted.

## Explicit decoding comparison on a common target

Use \(H=[1\ 1]\), \(s=1\), and \(w=(0,0)\), so both \(e=01\) and
\(e=10\) are optimal. The quadratic penalty
\(Q(e)=2J(e_1+e_2-1)^2\), with \(e_i=(z_i+1)/2\), is \(J+Jz_1z_2\).
It represents the required decoding problem faithfully for every \(J>0\).

Take a physical four-vertex path \(0-1-2-3\). The native embedding uses
singletons 1 and 2; the other embedding uses branches \(\{0,1\}\) and

temperature, control error, or preparation/ramp time is included. For a

preparation and ramps separately.

\[

   \sin^2\!\left(t\sqrt{J^2+4\Gamma^2}\right).
\]

\(1-\varepsilon(t)^2>0.983523\). Thus the direction of the performance

Hamiltonians, target, and pause duration. Larger chains inhibit repair but
protect an answer already present. This is a certified limitation on any
universal preference based only on chain size or final-energy equivalence.

This comparison uses a common problem-energy scale. Maximizing the available
problem scale separately in each embedding changes the Hamiltonians and can
change the comparison. The result does not claim native embeddings always
win or that chain count alone orders performance.

It represents the required decoding problem faithfully for every \(J>0\).

Take a physical four-vertex path \(0-1-2-3\). The native embedding uses
singletons 1 and 2; the other embedding uses branches \(\{0,1\}\) and
\(\{2,3\}\), with problem interaction on edge \(1-2\). Both have the
same logical problem coefficient \(J=10^{-4}\), transverse field
\(\Gamma=0.02\), field range \(|h|\leq1\), coupler range \(|J_{qr}|\leq1\),
and the same available target. Embedded chain couplings are \(-K=-1\).
A per-node absolute coupling-group cap of 2 suffices for both; any smaller
provided cap must be checked or the common scale changed. This is a parametric
programming model, not a claim about an exported Advantage2 processor. The
path can be selected from an ideal Zephyr target without adding edges.

Both are initialized in encoded \(e=00\) and held for
\(t=\pi/(2\sqrt{J^2+4\Gamma^2})\), about 39.27. No bath, decoherence,
temperature, control error, or preparation/ramp time is included. For a
reverse-anneal interpretation, these statements are conditional on the state
at the start of the pause. A complete anneal would require analyzing its
preparation and ramps separately.

The native Hamiltonian is
\(H_{\rm native}=JZ_1Z_2-\Gamma(X_1+X_2)\). An exact two-dimensional
bright/dark-state calculation yields

\[
 p_{\rm native}(t)={2\Gamma^2\over J^2+4\Gamma^2}
   \sin^2\!\left(t\sqrt{J^2+4\Gamma^2}\right).
\]

At the selected time this is approximately 0.499997. For the four-qubit
embedding, \(\Delta=2K=2\), \(R=J\), \(N=M=4\), \(n_1=0,n_2=2\),
so \(g=1.9198\), \(b=0.02\sqrt8\), and the theorem gives
\(p_{\rm encoded}\leq\varepsilon(t)^2<0.016477\). Thus the native mapping has
strictly greater finite-time decoding success under the stated protocol, proved
without simulating the embedded dynamics. The success projector includes
both tied optima. Exact simulation in the companion script checks the values.

For a second comparison change only the encoded initial state to an optimal
assignment \(e=01\). The native success probability is now
\(1-0.499996875\approx0.500003125\). Apply the zero-initial-event bound to
failure: the encoded success is at least
\(1-\varepsilon(t)^2>0.983523\). Thus the direction of the performance
ordering reverses under a change of initial state, with the same task,
Hamiltonians, target, and pause duration. Larger chains inhibit repair but
protect an answer already present. This is a certified limitation on any
universal preference based only on chain size or final-energy equivalence.

This comparison uses a common problem-energy scale. Maximizing the available
problem scale separately in each embedding changes the Hamiltonians and can
change the comparison. The result does not claim native embeddings always
win or that chain count alone orders performance.

## Reproduction and public resources

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 benchmarks/qec-annealing-embedding/labs/lab-002-agent-test-general-h/scripts/theory_checks.py
```

The script emits JSON with environment versions, the exact comparison, and
independent random-matrix checks. It accepts `--output PATH` to save those
results; it does not access another lab or scientific history.

Public resources consulted on 2026-10-07:

- D-Wave, [Annealing Implementation and Controls](https://docs.dwavequantum.com/en/latest/quantum_research/annealing.html),
  for the normalization of the transverse-field Hamiltonian and the distinction
  between pauses, reverse annealing, and complete schedules.
- S. Bravyi, D. DiVincenzo, and D. Loss,
  [Schrieffer-Wolff transformation for quantum many-body systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.0675),
  Ann. Phys. 326, 2793–2826 (2011), for context on block-unitary effective
  Hamiltonians. The explicit Sylvester/conjugation proof above is given in full;
  no undocumented constant is imported from this reference.
- V. Choi, [Minor-Embedding in Adiabatic Quantum Computation: I. The Parameter
  Setting Problem](https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.4884), for static minor-embedding
  context. Static parameter fidelity is distinct from theorem (1).

The global bandwidth separation \(\Delta>2R+\Gamma(N+n_1)\) is deliberately
conservative. It can fail for useful embeddings, and late holds cannot repair
all the limitations of an earlier anneal. General early-time or open-system
dynamics, a sharp ranking between long chains, and universal forward-anneal
success remain outside this result.

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /Users/home/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/Research/[Mercor]SciCode2/benchmarks/qec-annealing-embedding/labs/lab-002-agent-test-general-h/scripts/reviewer_witness_check.py
+"""Read saved witnesses without calling solver verification/allocation code."""
+from collections import defaultdict
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+from pathlib import Path
+import random
+
+LAB = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+RESULTS = LAB / "results"
+target = json.loads((RESULTS / "target_zephyr_g6.json").read_text())
+nodes = set(target["nodes"])
+edges = {tuple(sorted(edge)) for edge in target["edges"]}
+adjacency = defaultdict(set)
+for q, r in edges:
+    adjacency[q].add(r)
+    adjacency[r].add(q)
+rng = random.Random(731007)
+checks = []
+for path in sorted(RESULTS.glob("witness_*.json")):
+    witness = json.loads(path.read_text())
+    method = witness["method"]
+    name = path.stem.removeprefix("witness_").removesuffix("_" + method)
+    model = json.loads((RESULTS / ("model_" + name + ".json")).read_text())
+    branches = {int(i): list(branch) for i, branch in witness["embedding"].items()}
+    assert set(branches) == set(range(len(model["linear"])))
+    owner = {}
+    for i, branch in branches.items():
+        assert branch and len(set(branch)) == len(branch)
+        assert set(branch) <= nodes
+        for q in branch:
+            assert q not in owner
+            owner[q] = i
+        reached, pending = {branch[0]}, [branch[0]]
+        while pending:
+            q = pending.pop()
+            for r in adjacency[q] & set(branch) - reached:
+                reached.add(r)
+                pending.append(r)
+        assert reached == set(branch)
+    physical_h = dict(witness["h"])
+    physical_j = {tuple(sorted((q, r))): value for q, r, value in witness["J"]}
+    raw_h = dict(witness["h_raw"])
+    raw_j = {tuple(sorted((q, r))): value for q, r, value in witness["J_raw"]}
+    assert len(physical_h) == len(witness["h"]) and set(physical_h) == set(owner)
+    assert len(physical_j) == len(witness["J"]) and set(physical_j) <= edges
+    assert all(q in owner and r in owner for q, r in physical_j)
+    alpha = witness["scale"]

"""Read saved witnesses without calling solver verification/allocation code."""
from collections import defaultdict
import hashlib
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import random

LAB = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RESULTS = LAB / "results"
target = json.loads((RESULTS / "target_zephyr_g6.json").read_text())
nodes = set(target["nodes"])
edges = {tuple(sorted(edge)) for edge in target["edges"]}
adjacency = defaultdict(set)
for q, r in edges:
    adjacency[q].add(r)
    adjacency[r].add(q)
rng = random.Random(731007)
checks = []
for path in sorted(RESULTS.glob("witness_*.json")):
    witness = json.loads(path.read_text())
    method = witness["method"]
    name = path.stem.removeprefix("witness_").removesuffix("_" + method)
    model = json.loads((RESULTS / ("model_" + name + ".json")).read_text())
    branches = {int(i): list(branch) for i, branch in witness["embedding"].items()}
    assert set(branches) == set(range(len(model["linear"])))
    owner = {}
    for i, branch in branches.items():
        assert branch and len(set(branch)) == len(branch)
        assert set(branch) <= nodes
        for q in branch:
            assert q not in owner
            owner[q] = i
        reached, pending = {branch[0]}, [branch[0]]
        while pending:
            q = pending.pop()
            for r in adjacency[q] & set(branch) - reached:
                reached.add(r)
                pending.append(r)
        assert reached == set(branch)
    physical_h = dict(witness["h"])
    physical_j = {tuple(sorted((q, r))): value for q, r, value in witness["J"]}
    raw_h = dict(witness["h_raw"])
    raw_j = {tuple(sorted((q, r))): value for q, r, value in witness["J_raw"]}
    assert len(physical_h) == len(witness["h"]) and set(physical_h) == set(owner)
    assert len(physical_j) == len(witness["J"]) and set(physical_j) <= edges
    assert all(q in owner and r in owner for q, r in physical_j)
    alpha = witness["scale"]
    assert alpha > 0
    assert all(math.isclose(physical_h[q], alpha * value, rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=1e-12) for q, value in raw_h.items())
    assert all(math.isclose(physical_j[edge], alpha * value, rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=1e-12) for edge, value in raw_j.items())
    lo, hi = witness["ranges"]["h"]
    assert all(lo - 1e-12 <= v <= hi + 1e-12 for v in physical_h.values())
    lo, hi = witness["ranges"]["J"]
    assert all(lo - 1e-12 <= v <= hi + 1e-12 for v in physical_j.values())
    lo, hi = witness["ranges"]["coupling_group"]
    for group in target["coupling_groups"]:
        value = math.fsum(physical_j.get(tuple(sorted(edge)), 0) for edge in group)
        assert lo - 1e-12 <= value <= hi + 1e-12
    logical_h = {i: v / 2 for i, v in enumerate(model["linear"])}
    logical_j = {}
    logical_offset = model["offset"] + math.fsum(model["linear"]) / 2
    for i, j, value in model["quadratic"]:
        logical_h[i] += value / 4
        logical_h[j] += value / 4
        logical_j[(i, j)] = value / 4
        logical_offset += value / 4
        assert any(tuple(sorted((q, r))) in edges for q in branches[i] for r in branches[j])
    allocated_h, allocated_j = defaultdict(float), defaultdict(float)
    for q, value in raw_h.items():
        allocated_h[owner[q]] += value
    for (q, r), value in raw_j.items():
        if owner[q] != owner[r]:
            allocated_j[tuple(sorted((owner[q], owner[r])))] += value
    assert all(math.isclose(allocated_h[i], v, abs_tol=1e-9) for i, v in logical_h.items())
    assert set(allocated_j) == set(logical_j)
    assert all(math.isclose(allocated_j[edge], v, abs_tol=1e-9) for edge, v in logical_j.items())
    for i, branch in branches.items():
        chain_edges = witness["chain_edges"][str(i)]
        assert len(chain_edges) == len(branch) - 1
        if chain_edges:
            load = abs(logical_h[i]) + sum(abs(v) for (j, k), v in logical_j.items() if i in (j, k))
            strength = witness["chain_strength_raw"][str(i)]
            assert strength > load
            assert all(math.isclose(raw_j[tuple(sorted(edge))], -strength, abs_tol=1e-9) for edge in chain_edges)
    max_error = 0
    for _ in range(32):
        y = [rng.randrange(2) for _ in model["linear"]]
        spins = {q: 2 * y[i] - 1 for q, i in owner.items()}
        qubo_energy = model["offset"] + math.fsum(v * y[i] for i, v in enumerate(model["linear"]))
        qubo_energy += math.fsum(v * y[i] * y[j] for i, j, v in model["quadratic"])
        physical_energy = witness["offset"] + math.fsum(v * spins[q] for q, v in physical_h.items())
        physical_energy += math.fsum(v * spins[q] * spins[r] for (q, r), v in physical_j.items())
        error = abs(physical_energy - alpha * qubo_energy)
        max_error = max(max_error, error)
        assert error < 1e-9
    checks.append({"path": str(path.relative_to(LAB)), "sha256": hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                   "physical_qubits": len(owner), "consistent_states_checked": 32,
                   "max_scaled_energy_error": max_error})
result = {"status": "pass", "role": "independent coordinator review of saved witnesses only",
          "witnesses": len(checks), "seed": 731007, "checks": checks,
          "scope": "Branch validity, actual interactions, coefficient allocation, chain sufficient condition, ranges/group limits, scaled consistent-state energies. No numerical simulation of large physical ground states."}
(RESULTS / "reviewer-witness-check.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps({"status": result["status"], "witnesses": len(checks),
                  "consistent_states_checked": 32 * len(checks),
                  "max_scaled_energy_error": max(x["max_scaled_energy_error"] for x in checks)}, indent=2))

"""Sparse binary parity constraints -> bounded-size XOR-chain QUBO.

No decoding optimization is performed during compilation. Arithmetic in the
proof is exact; this implementation uses finite IEEE doubles and rejects
non-finite coefficients. JSON output contains every variable, including isolates.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import math
import copy
from fractions import Fraction
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import networkx as nx


def normalize_rows(rows, n):
    """Canonicalize sparse row supports; repeated coordinates add over GF(2)."""
    out = []
    for row in rows:
        row = list(row)
        if any(int(i) != i for i in row):
            raise ValueError("Column indices must be integers")
        counts = Counter(int(i) for i in row)
        if any(i < 0 or i >= n for i in counts):
            raise ValueError("Column index outside [0,n)")
        out.append(sorted(i for i, count in counts.items() if count % 2))
    return out


def _ratio(x):
    return [x.numerator, x.denominator]


def certify_coefficients(model, exact_linear, exact_quadratic, exact_offset,
                         require_float_fidelity=True):
    """A rational rounding-error certificate for IEEE coefficient output.

    Finite binary64 inputs have exact rational values. Their objective costs
    lie on a rational lattice. Compare the exact lattice/penalty gap with twice
    the total coefficient error. Offsets do not affect ground states.
    """
    weights = [Fraction(w) for w in model["weights"]]
    exact_budget = sum(map(abs,weights), Fraction(0))
    margin = Fraction(model["penalty"])-exact_budget
    if margin <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Penalty does not strictly exceed exact weight L1 norm")
    denominator = max((w.denominator for w in weights),default=1)
    numerator_gcd = math.gcd(*(abs(w.numerator)*(denominator//w.denominator) for w in weights))
    lattice = Fraction(numerator_gcd,denominator) if numerator_gcd else None
    gap = min(margin,lattice) if lattice else margin
    approx_quad={(i,j):Fraction(q) for i,j,q in model["quadratic"]}
    rho = sum((abs(Fraction(a)-b) for a,b in zip(model["linear"],exact_linear)),Fraction(0))
    rho += sum((abs(approx_quad.get(pair,Fraction(0))-b) for pair,b in exact_quadratic.items()),Fraction(0))
    certified = 2*rho < gap
    model["exact_coefficients"] = {
        "linear": [_ratio(a) for a in exact_linear],
        "quadratic": [[i,j,*_ratio(q)] for (i,j),q in sorted(exact_quadratic.items()) if q],
        "offset": _ratio(exact_offset),
        "interpretation": "authoritative exact rational model for the binary64 input weights and penalty"}
    model["numeric_certificate"] = {
        "float_ground_states_certified": certified,
        "coefficient_error_l1_exact": _ratio(rho),
        "nonoptimal_gap_lower_bound_exact": _ratio(gap),
        "weight_lattice_step_exact": None if lattice is None else _ratio(lattice),
        "exact_penalty_margin": _ratio(margin),
        "offset_error_exact": _ratio(abs(Fraction(model["offset"])-exact_offset)),
        "condition": "2 * coefficient_error_l1 < nonoptimal_gap_lower_bound"}
    if require_float_fidelity and not certified:
        raise ArithmeticError("Floating expansion cannot be certified faithful; use require_float_fidelity=False to obtain authoritative exact rational coefficients")
    return model


def compile_instance(rows, n, syndrome, weights, penalty=None, require_float_fidelity=True):
    """Return faithful sparse QUBO, assuming syndrome lies in image(H).

    penalty must strictly exceed sum(abs(weights)). Set a fixed envelope for
    repeated syndromes/weights to avoid rebuilding the structural coefficients.
    y_i=(z_i+1)/2 is the Ising conversion used by the companion implementation.
    """
    if n < 0 or int(n) != n:
        raise ValueError("n must be a nonnegative integer")
    rows = normalize_rows(rows, n)
    syndrome = list(syndrome)
    if any(s not in (0,1) for s in syndrome):
        raise ValueError("Syndrome entries must be binary")
    syndrome = [int(s) for s in syndrome]
    weights = [float(w) for w in weights]
    if len(rows) != len(syndrome) or len(weights) != n:
        raise ValueError("Dimension mismatch")
    if any(s not in (0, 1) for s in syndrome):
        raise ValueError("Syndrome entries must be binary")
    if not all(math.isfinite(w) for w in weights):
        raise ValueError("Weights must be finite")
    budget = math.fsum(abs(w) for w in weights)
    penalty = float(budget + 1.0 if penalty is None else penalty)
    if not math.isfinite(penalty) or not penalty > budget:
        raise ValueError("Need finite penalty > sum(abs(weights)); supply a larger envelope")
    linear = list(weights)
    exact_linear = list(map(Fraction,weights))
    quadratic = defaultdict(float)
    exact_quadratic = defaultdict(Fraction)
    offset = 0.0
    exact_offset = Fraction(0)
    exact_penalty = Fraction(penalty)
    variables = [{"kind": "error", "column": i} for i in range(n)]
    constraints = []
    structural_edges = set()

    def auxiliary(kind, row, stage):
        variables.append({"kind": kind, "row": row, "stage": stage})
        linear.append(0.0)
        exact_linear.append(Fraction(0))
        return len(linear) - 1

    def square(coeffs, constant, row, kind):
        nonlocal offset,exact_offset
        terms = sorted(coeffs.items())
        for i, a in terms:
            linear[i] += penalty * (a*a + 2*constant*a)
            exact_linear[i] += exact_penalty*(a*a+2*constant*a)
        for p, (i, a) in enumerate(terms):
            for j, b in terms[p+1:]:
                quadratic[i, j] += 2*penalty*a*b
                exact_quadratic[i,j] += 2*exact_penalty*a*b
                structural_edges.add((i, j))
        offset += penalty*constant*constant
        exact_offset += exact_penalty*constant*constant
        constraints.append({"row": row, "kind": kind,
                            "terms": [[i, a] for i, a in terms],
                            "constant": constant})

    for r, (support, s) in enumerate(zip(rows, syndrome)):
        d = len(support)
        if d == 0:
            if s:
                raise ValueError("Empty check has nonzero syndrome (infeasible)")
        elif d == 1:
            square({support[0]: 1}, -s, r, "final")
        else:
            previous = support[0]
            for stage, current in enumerate(support[1:]):
                if stage == d-2:
                    # Exact degree-two parity violation indicator, avoiding the
                    # final carry. Its interaction sign depends on syndrome.
                    sign = 1-2*s
                    linear[previous] += penalty*sign
                    linear[current] += penalty*sign
                    exact_linear[previous] += exact_penalty*sign
                    exact_linear[current] += exact_penalty*sign
                    pair = tuple(sorted((previous, current)))
                    quadratic[pair] -= 2*penalty*sign
                    exact_quadratic[pair] -= 2*exact_penalty*sign
                    structural_edges.add(pair)
                    offset += penalty*s
                    exact_offset += exact_penalty*s
                    constraints.append({"row": r, "kind": "parity",
                                        "inputs": [previous, current], "target": s})
                else:
                    carry = auxiliary("carry", r, stage)
                    parity = auxiliary("prefix", r, stage)
                    square({previous: 1, current: 1, parity: -1, carry: -2}, 0, r, "xor")
                    previous = parity

    quadratic = [[i, j, q] for (i, j), q in sorted(quadratic.items()) if q != 0]
    if not all(math.isfinite(c) for c in linear + [offset] + [q[2] for q in quadratic]):
        raise ValueError("Coefficient overflow")
    model = {"schema": "xor-chain-qubo-v1", "n_original": n, "rows": rows,
            "syndrome": syndrome, "weights": weights, "penalty": penalty,
            "weight_l1": budget, "linear": linear, "quadratic": quadratic,
            "offset": offset, "variables": variables, "constraints": constraints,
            "structural_edges": [list(edge) for edge in sorted(structural_edges)]}
    return certify_coefficients(model,exact_linear,exact_quadratic,exact_offset,require_float_fidelity)


def model_graph(model, structural=False):
    graph = nx.Graph()
    graph.add_nodes_from(range(len(model["linear"])))
    if structural:
        graph.add_edges_from(model["structural_edges"])
    else:
        graph.add_edges_from((i, j) for i, j, q in model["quadratic"] if q)
    return graph


def energy(model, y):
    return (model["offset"] + math.fsum(c*int(y[i]) for i, c in enumerate(model["linear"]))
            + math.fsum(q*int(y[i])*int(y[j]) for i, j, q in model["quadratic"]))


def residual_energy(model, y):
    return (math.fsum(w*int(y[i]) for i, w in enumerate(model["weights"]))
            + model["penalty"]*sum(constraint_violation(c, y)
                                   for c in model["constraints"]))


def constraint_violation(c, y):
    if c["kind"] == "parity":
        return int((int(y[c["inputs"][0]]) ^ int(y[c["inputs"][1]])) != c["target"])
    return (c["constant"] + sum(a*int(y[i]) for i, a in c["terms"]))**2


def feasible(model, e):
    return all(sum(int(e[i]) for i in row) % 2 == s
               for row, s in zip(model["rows"], model["syndrome"]))


def complete_feasible(model, e):
    """Unique zero-penalty auxiliary extension of a feasible error pattern."""
    if len(e) != model["n_original"] or any(int(b) not in (0, 1) for b in e):
        raise ValueError("Error pattern dimension/bits invalid")
    if not feasible(model, e):
        raise ValueError("Error pattern does not match syndrome")
    y = list(map(int, e)) + [0]*(len(model["linear"])-len(e))
    for c in model["constraints"]:
        if c["kind"] == "xor":
            inputs = [i for i, a in c["terms"] if a == 1]
            carry = next(i for i, a in c["terms"] if a == -2)
            parity = next(i for i, a in c["terms"] if a == -1)
            total = sum(y[i] for i in inputs)
            y[carry], y[parity] = total//2, total % 2
    assert all(constraint_violation(c, y) == 0 for c in model["constraints"])
    return y


def update_instance(model, syndrome=None, weights=None, require_float_fidelity=True):
    """Numerical-only update in O(nnz(H)+n+m), including copying the output.

    Only final parity factors depend on syndrome. The preprocessed structural
    envelope survives cancellations/sign changes of actual quadratic terms.
    """
    syndrome = list(model["syndrome"] if syndrome is None else syndrome)
    weights = [float(w) for w in (model["weights"] if weights is None else weights)]
    if len(syndrome) != len(model["rows"]) or any(s not in (0,1) for s in syndrome):
        raise ValueError("Syndrome dimensions/bits invalid")
    if len(weights) != model["n_original"] or not all(math.isfinite(w) for w in weights):
        raise ValueError("Weight dimensions/values invalid")
    budget = math.fsum(abs(w) for w in weights)
    if not model["penalty"] > budget:
        raise ValueError("Updated weights exceed fixed penalty envelope")
    if any(not row and s for row,s in zip(model["rows"],syndrome)):
        raise ValueError("Empty check has nonzero syndrome (infeasible)")
    out = copy.deepcopy(model)
    M = model["penalty"]
    qdict = {(i,j): q for i,j,q in model["quadratic"]}
    exact_linear = [Fraction(*a) for a in model["exact_coefficients"]["linear"]]
    exact_quadratic = {(i,j): Fraction(a,b) for i,j,a,b in model["exact_coefficients"]["quadratic"]}
    exact_offset = Fraction(*model["exact_coefficients"]["offset"])
    exact_M = Fraction(M)
    for i,(old,new) in enumerate(zip(model["weights"],weights)):
        out["linear"][i] += new-old
        exact_linear[i] += Fraction(new)-Fraction(old)
    for c in out["constraints"]:
        r = c["row"]
        delta = syndrome[r]-model["syndrome"][r]
        if not delta or c["kind"] == "xor":
            continue
        out["offset"] += M*delta
        exact_offset += exact_M*delta
        if c["kind"] == "parity":
            a,b = c["inputs"]
            out["linear"][a] -= 2*M*delta
            out["linear"][b] -= 2*M*delta
            exact_linear[a] -= 2*exact_M*delta
            exact_linear[b] -= 2*exact_M*delta
            pair = tuple(sorted((a,b)))
            qdict[pair] = qdict.get(pair,0.0)+4*M*delta
            exact_quadratic[pair] = exact_quadratic.get(pair,Fraction(0))+4*exact_M*delta
            c["target"] = syndrome[r]
        else:
            assert len(c["terms"]) == 1
            a = c["terms"][0][0]
            out["linear"][a] -= 2*M*delta
            exact_linear[a] -= 2*exact_M*delta
            c["constant"] = -syndrome[r]
    out["quadratic"] = [[a,b,qdict[a,b]] for a,b in model["structural_edges"]
                        if qdict.get((a,b),0.0) != 0]
    out["syndrome"],out["weights"],out["weight_l1"] = syndrome,weights,budget
    return certify_coefficients(out,exact_linear,exact_quadratic,exact_offset,require_float_fidelity)

    if any(s not in (0,1) for s in syndrome):
        raise ValueError("Syndrome entries must be binary")
    syndrome = [int(s) for s in syndrome]
    weights = [float(w) for w in weights]
    if len(rows) != len(syndrome) or len(weights) != n:
        raise ValueError("Dimension mismatch")
    if any(s not in (0, 1) for s in syndrome):
        raise ValueError("Syndrome entries must be binary")
    if not all(math.isfinite(w) for w in weights):
        raise ValueError("Weights must be finite")
    budget = math.fsum(abs(w) for w in weights)
    penalty = float(budget + 1.0 if penalty is None else penalty)
    if not math.isfinite(penalty) or not penalty > budget:
        raise ValueError("Need finite penalty > sum(abs(weights)); supply a larger envelope")
    linear = list(weights)
    exact_linear = list(map(Fraction,weights))
    quadratic = defaultdict(float)
    exact_quadratic = defaultdict(Fraction)
    offset = 0.0
    exact_offset = Fraction(0)
    exact_penalty = Fraction(penalty)
    variables = [{"kind": "error", "column": i} for i in range(n)]
    constraints = []
    structural_edges = set()

    def auxiliary(kind, row, stage):
        variables.append({"kind": kind, "row": row, "stage": stage})
        linear.append(0.0)
        exact_linear.append(Fraction(0))
        return len(linear) - 1

    def square(coeffs, constant, row, kind):
        nonlocal offset,exact_offset
        terms = sorted(coeffs.items())
        for i, a in terms:
            linear[i] += penalty * (a*a + 2*constant*a)
            exact_linear[i] += exact_penalty*(a*a+2*constant*a)
        for p, (i, a) in enumerate(terms):
            for j, b in terms[p+1:]:
                quadratic[i, j] += 2*penalty*a*b
                exact_quadratic[i,j] += 2*exact_penalty*a*b
                structural_edges.add((i, j))
        offset += penalty*constant*constant
        exact_offset += exact_penalty*constant*constant
        constraints.append({"row": row, "kind": kind,
                            "terms": [[i, a] for i, a in terms],
                            "constant": constant})

    for r, (support, s) in enumerate(zip(rows, syndrome)):
        d = len(support)
        if d == 0:
            if s:
                raise ValueError("Empty check has nonzero syndrome (infeasible)")
        elif d == 1:
            square({support[0]: 1}, -s, r, "final")
        else:
            previous = support[0]
            for stage, current in enumerate(support[1:]):
                if stage == d-2:
                    # Exact degree-two parity violation indicator, avoiding the
                    # final carry. Its interaction sign depends on syndrome.
                    sign = 1-2*s
                    linear[previous] += penalty*sign
                    linear[current] += penalty*sign
                    exact_linear[previous] += exact_penalty*sign
                    exact_linear[current] += exact_penalty*sign
                    pair = tuple(sorted((previous, current)))
                    quadratic[pair] -= 2*penalty*sign
                    exact_quadratic[pair] -= 2*exact_penalty*sign
                    structural_edges.add(pair)
                    offset += penalty*s
                    exact_offset += exact_penalty*s
                    constraints.append({"row": r, "kind": "parity",
                                        "inputs": [previous, current], "target": s})
                else:
                    carry = auxiliary("carry", r, stage)
                    parity = auxiliary("prefix", r, stage)
                    square({previous: 1, current: 1, parity: -1, carry: -2}, 0, r, "xor")
                    previous = parity

    quadratic = [[i, j, q] for (i, j), q in sorted(quadratic.items()) if q != 0]
    if not all(math.isfinite(c) for c in linear + [offset] + [q[2] for q in quadratic]):
        raise ValueError("Coefficient overflow")
    model = {"schema": "xor-chain-qubo-v1", "n_original": n, "rows": rows,
            "syndrome": syndrome, "weights": weights, "penalty": penalty,
            "weight_l1": budget, "linear": linear, "quadratic": quadratic,
            "offset": offset, "variables": variables, "constraints": constraints,
            "structural_edges": [list(edge) for edge in sorted(structural_edges)]}
    return certify_coefficients(model,exact_linear,exact_quadratic,exact_offset,require_float_fidelity)


def model_graph(model, structural=False):
    graph = nx.Graph()
    graph.add_nodes_from(range(len(model["linear"])))
    if structural:
        graph.add_edges_from(model["structural_edges"])
    else:
        graph.add_edges_from((i, j) for i, j, q in model["quadratic"] if q)
    return graph


def energy(model, y):
    return (model["offset"] + math.fsum(c*int(y[i]) for i, c in enumerate(model["linear"]))
            + math.fsum(q*int(y[i])*int(y[j]) for i, j, q in model["quadratic"]))


def residual_energy(model, y):
    return (math.fsum(w*int(y[i]) for i, w in enumerate(model["weights"]))
            + model["penalty"]*sum(constraint_violation(c, y)
                                   for c in model["constraints"]))


def constraint_violation(c, y):
    if c["kind"] == "parity":
        return int((int(y[c["inputs"][0]]) ^ int(y[c["inputs"][1]])) != c["target"])
    return (c["constant"] + sum(a*int(y[i]) for i, a in c["terms"]))**2


def feasible(model, e):
    return all(sum(int(e[i]) for i in row) % 2 == s
               for row, s in zip(model["rows"], model["syndrome"]))


def complete_feasible(model, e):
    """Unique zero-penalty auxiliary extension of a feasible error pattern."""
    if len(e) != model["n_original"] or any(int(b) not in (0, 1) for b in e):
        raise ValueError("Error pattern dimension/bits invalid")
    if not feasible(model, e):
        raise ValueError("Error pattern does not match syndrome")
    y = list(map(int, e)) + [0]*(len(model["linear"])-len(e))
    for c in model["constraints"]:
        if c["kind"] == "xor":
            inputs = [i for i, a in c["terms"] if a == 1]
            carry = next(i for i, a in c["terms"] if a == -2)
            parity = next(i for i, a in c["terms"] if a == -1)
            total = sum(y[i] for i in inputs)
            y[carry], y[parity] = total//2, total % 2
    assert all(constraint_violation(c, y) == 0 for c in model["constraints"])
    return y


def update_instance(model, syndrome=None, weights=None, require_float_fidelity=True):
    """Numerical-only update in O(nnz(H)+n+m), including copying the output.

    Only final parity factors depend on syndrome. The preprocessed structural
    envelope survives cancellations/sign changes of actual quadratic terms.
    """
    syndrome = list(model["syndrome"] if syndrome is None else syndrome)
    weights = [float(w) for w in (model["weights"] if weights is None else weights)]
    if len(syndrome) != len(model["rows"]) or any(s not in (0,1) for s in syndrome):
        raise ValueError("Syndrome dimensions/bits invalid")
    if len(weights) != model["n_original"] or not all(math.isfinite(w) for w in weights):
        raise ValueError("Weight dimensions/values invalid")
    budget = math.fsum(abs(w) for w in weights)
    if not model["penalty"] > budget:
        raise ValueError("Updated weights exceed fixed penalty envelope")
    if any(not row and s for row,s in zip(model["rows"],syndrome)):
        raise ValueError("Empty check has nonzero syndrome (infeasible)")
    out = copy.deepcopy(model)
    M = model["penalty"]
    qdict = {(i,j): q for i,j,q in model["quadratic"]}
    exact_linear = [Fraction(*a) for a in model["exact_coefficients"]["linear"]]
    exact_quadratic = {(i,j): Fraction(a,b) for i,j,a,b in model["exact_coefficients"]["quadratic"]}
    exact_offset = Fraction(*model["exact_coefficients"]["offset"])
    exact_M = Fraction(M)
    for i,(old,new) in enumerate(zip(model["weights"],weights)):
        out["linear"][i] += new-old
        exact_linear[i] += Fraction(new)-Fraction(old)
    for c in out["constraints"]:
        r = c["row"]
        delta = syndrome[r]-model["syndrome"][r]
        if not delta or c["kind"] == "xor":
            continue
        out["offset"] += M*delta
        exact_offset += exact_M*delta
        if c["kind"] == "parity":
            a,b = c["inputs"]
            out["linear"][a] -= 2*M*delta
            out["linear"][b] -= 2*M*delta
            exact_linear[a] -= 2*exact_M*delta
            exact_linear[b] -= 2*exact_M*delta
            pair = tuple(sorted((a,b)))
            qdict[pair] = qdict.get(pair,0.0)+4*M*delta
            exact_quadratic[pair] = exact_quadratic.get(pair,Fraction(0))+4*exact_M*delta
            c["target"] = syndrome[r]
        else:
            assert len(c["terms"]) == 1
            a = c["terms"][0][0]
            out["linear"][a] -= 2*M*delta
            exact_linear[a] -= 2*exact_M*delta
            c["constant"] = -syndrome[r]
    out["quadratic"] = [[a,b,qdict[a,b]] for a,b in model["structural_edges"]
                        if qdict.get((a,b),0.0) != 0]
    out["syndrome"],out["weights"],out["weight_l1"] = syndrome,weights,budget
    return certify_coefficients(out,exact_linear,exact_quadratic,exact_offset,require_float_fidelity)
"}

# Target construction, embedding, and programming notes

This note records the embedding subtask of this autonomous run. It used only the
run prompt, public sources, and artifacts newly written in this run. The target
is an **ideal** Zephyr graph, not an exported device working graph. The installed
generator is `dwave_networkx.zephyr_graph` 0.8.18, the predecessor of the current
`dwave.graphs.zephyr_graph` name. Every saved witness includes all target nodes,
edges, generator version, and parameters. The environment also has minorminer
0.2.21, dwave-system 1.34.0, dimod 0.12.21, networkx 3.5, and Python 3.13.2.

## Explicit polynomial construction

`CliqueTemplate(target, engine="tracks")` is the default. For integer-labeled,
ideal `Z_(g,4)` with `g>=2`, it constructs the published track embedding of
`K_(16g+1)` from Section 5.1 of [Boothby, King, and Raymond, *Zephyr Topology of
D-Wave Quantum Processors*, 2021](https://www.dwavequantum.com/media/2uznec4s/14-1056a-a_zephyr_topology_of_d-wave_quantum_processors.pdf).
A track `(u,w,k,j)` contains every `(u,w,k,j,z)` for `0<=z<g`. The branch
descriptors are implemented literally as A--E in `embedding.py`. Two branches
have length `g`; the other `16g-1` have length `2g`. Thus this complete template
uses exactly `32g^2` qubits, within the target's `32g^2+16g` qubits. This is a
known construction, not a claimed new clique-embedding result.

Here is a direct validity argument for the descriptors. External couplers join
each track. Every vertical interior track (`1<=w<=2g-1`) meets every horizontal
interior track, as follows by choosing the internal-coupler indices in the
published coordinate rule. A peripheral `w=0` track meets the opposite tracks
whose shift is zero. In descriptors B and E each branch has both orientations
of interior tracks. Descriptors C and D have one interior zero-shift track and
one perpendicular peripheral track. The two A branches are the two zero-shift
interior tracks at `w=3,k=0`. These observations give an internal connection
within each two-track branch and a contact for each pair of branches. The
descriptor ranges partition their tracks: B uses interior `w=1,2` with shift
one, C and D use the peripheral tracks and the remaining shift-zero tracks at
`w=1,2`, and E uses `w>=3`, excluding the two A tracks. Thus branch sets are
disjoint. Each constructed template is additionally checked against the exact
generated target graph before use.

For `g=1`, the code explicitly contracts a matching of the interior `K_(8,8)`:
branch `2k+j` contains `(0,1,k,j,0)` and `(1,1,k,j,0)` for `k=0,...,3`,
`j=0,1`. This gives a checked `K_8` using 16 qubits. There is no assertion that
these capacities are maximum minors. Inputs beyond capacity may still fit.

The track construction emits `O(g^2)` qubits. The ideal target has bounded
degree 20 and `O(g^2)` edges. Branch-tree construction, full clique verification,
and extraction of one contact for each logical pair each take `O(g^2)` time and
memory. The implementation traverses integer target labels and sorts only
bounded-degree neighbor lists, so it does not need a global edge sort in this
path. Serialization may separately sort witness lists. These are arithmetic
operation counts; rational bit complexity must be charged separately.

`engine="native"` retains the practical Ocean clique routine
`minorminer.busclique.find_clique_embedding(...,use_cache=False,seed=...)`.
Its default sufficient capacity is `16g-8` and observed branches are shorter.
The explicit path establishes the construction bound; the native path is an
optional measured library baseline. The [Ocean clique documentation](https://docs.dwavequantum.com/en/latest/ocean/api_ref_minorminer/source/clique_embedding.html)
describes native clique search and its caching interface. No persistent cache
was used in the measured native runs.

## Universal restriction and pruning

Once a complete template is checked, every integer-labeled graph with at most
its capacity embeds by assigning variables in sorted order to its first branch
sets. This includes isolated variables. The graph is the actual nonzero
quadratic interaction graph, not the check incidence graph.

Preprocessing fixes a spanning tree for each branch and one contact edge for
every template pair. For a new graph, mark the endpoints of the contact edges
needed by its interactions; remove nonterminal leaves from each branch tree.
An isolated variable keeps one qubit. The remaining tree is the unique minimal
subtree of the chosen tree spanning its terminals. It is nonempty and connected,
contains all required contacts, remains disjoint from other branches, and uses
no more qubits than the original branch. This proves validity and resource
nonincrease relative to this template; it does not compare quantum dynamics.

For `N` source variables, `M` interactions, and `Q<=2gN` selected full-template
qubits, a query costs `O(N log N + Q + M)` time and `O(Q+M)` working/output space.
Its logical ordering can be retained across updates. Repeated syndrome/weight
instances with unchanged graph need no new embedding query. The same reuse is
also available to any previously successful automatic embedding. If H or the
variable graph changes, a fresh query is guaranteed within capacity; a larger
graph requires another declared target/template or a search. A damaged target
must be revalidated and may invalidate the template.

`find_automatic_embedding` calls the general `minorminer.find_embedding`, then
places isolated variables and independently checks the result. Exceeding target
node/edge counts is a certified counting obstruction. An exhausted search,
insufficient leftover isolate space in a found partial embedding, or exceeding
template capacity is **not** a proof that the input has no minor embedding.

## Physical allocation and fidelity

The convention is `x_i=(1+z_i)/2`. The exact Ising conversion preserves constants.
Fields are shared uniformly over a branch; each logical coupler is placed on one
deterministically chosen available contact. Every branch has a BFS tree with
ferromagnetic coupling `-K_i`. Define

`L_i=|h_i|+sum_j |J_ij|`, and choose `K_i=chain_factor*L_i+chain_margin`

with `chain_factor>=1` and positive `chain_margin`. The physical offset is the
logical offset plus the sum of `K_i` over tree edges. Consequently the raw
physical energy of every consistent assignment equals the logical energy.

If a branch is broken, choose one monochromatic component of its tree and flip
the whole component. Every incident tree wall disappears, improving chain energy
by at least `2K_i`. The change of all nonchain terms incident to this component
is at most `2L_i`. Thus some change strictly lowers energy by at least
`2(K_i-L_i)`, and no broken state can be a global ground state. Applying this
argument until consistent proves physical ground-state fidelity. If the exact
logical nonoptimal gap is bounded below by `delta_Q`, the exact raw physical
nonoptimal gap is at least

`min(delta_Q, 2 min_(nonsingleton i)(K_i-L_i))`.

The minimum over no nonsingleton branches is omitted. The argument permits
degenerate optima and does not assume a unique correction.

All fields, logical couplers, reduction penalties, and chain couplers enter a
common positive scale `alpha`. The code supports asymmetric intervals for h and
J and signed sums of coupling strengths in the Zephyr groups generated by
`dwave.system.coupling_groups`. The [official solver-property description](https://docs.dwavequantum.com/en/latest/quantum_research/solver_properties_all.html)
states these are separate constraints. The defaults `h=(-4,4)`, `J=(-1,1)`,
and groups `(-13,10)` are illustrative parameter choices, not claimed properties
of a particular QPU. No device export was available. All alternatives in a
comparison must use the same target and these same chosen intervals. For other
Zephyr tile sizes, callers must supply the correct coupling groups explicitly.

`allocate_physical_exact` builds an exact companion from the compiler's rational
coefficients. The chosen binary64 K values and alpha are treated as exact rational
parameters, and their positive margin is checked against exact logical loads.
Let rho be the sum of absolute errors of all actual programmed h and J values
relative to that companion. If `2 rho < alpha*delta_raw`, every rounded ground
state belongs to the exact ground set. This is the elementary uniform diagonal
energy perturbation bound; it allows selection within a tied optimum. Constant
offset error is recorded but does not affect minimizers. Actual binary64 h/J and
group sums are checked using exact rational arithmetic. If necessary, alpha is
moved toward zero with `nextafter` to make every programmed constraint hold.
Failure of the sufficient fidelity certificate is explicit and means
inconclusive, not proof that the physical minimizers are wrong.

The allocator currently scans the target and groups on every program update:
`O(|E_T|+Q+M)` arithmetic work on ideal Zephyr, with rational error-certificate
work linear in programmed coefficients and group incidences. It does not claim
that these scans are already reduced to the changed weights alone. Contacts,
trees, and group membership could be cached further. This is one limitation of
the implementation's update cost.

## Checks, evidence, and limitations

`results/embed_explicit_tracks_checks.json` verifies explicit complete minors for
g=1,2,3,4,6,8,12. `embed_explicit_tracks_witness.json` contains the entire g=6
target and K97 template. Observed template preprocessing was about 20 ms at g=6
and 96 ms at g=12 in the first run; timings are observations, not asymptotic
proofs. The g=6 complete template has 1152 qubits and maximum branch length 12.

`results/embed_checks.json` records all 1024 graphs on five vertices surviving
template pruning, six kinds of invalid embeddings rejected, 496 QUBO-to-Ising
assignment checks, and physical consistency/ground-state checks on small models.
`embed_physical_witness.json` is an independently inspectable small programmed
model. Additional exact numeric-certificate checks are recorded in the same file.

The separate `embed_benchmark.json` and `embed_target_and_witnesses.json` preserve
the initial nine-graph **native-template** experiment on the same ideal g=4
target, with three seeded automatic reference runs per graph. Graphs include
paths, random cubic graphs, and seeded Erdos-Renyi graphs of 24,40,56 variables.
Native full-template counts were 120,200,280 respectively. Pruned counts ranged
37--246; automatic outputs ranged 24--244. Automatic embedding usually used
fewer physical qubits, while pruned-template queries were faster. Template
queries exclude independent revalidation, whereas the recorded automatic call
includes it; both timing components are given. No claim of overall quality or
annealing superiority follows from these observations. Parent-run matrix
experiments provide the decoding-specific comparison.

Two initial invocations of the uncached native clique routine at g=1 stalled
and later exited with code 137; the precise cause was not diagnosed. This
affected exploratory checks, not saved successful timings. The explicit g=1
construction above avoids that call. The g>=2 native runs completed normally.

Reproduce these checks without credentials:

```sh
python /absolute/path/to/lab/scripts/embedding_checks.py --output /absolute/path/to/lab/results
```

The guarantees concern valid minors, faithful final classical ground states,
explicit programming constraints, finite-precision certification, and
resource/processing costs. Any annealing-path theorem is separate; a smaller
branch count, shorter chain, or larger final-energy scale alone does not prove
better finite-time quantum-annealing success.
class CliqueTemplate:
    """Precompute one checked clique minor and fixed contacts for every pair.

    For a fixed verified target/template, every graph with N <= capacity is
    guaranteed a valid embedding.  Capacity failure says nothing about whether
    a different embedding fits.  With prune=True, keep the unique minimal
    subtree of the fixed branch tree spanning this input graph's contacts.
    """
    def __init__(self, target, capacity=None, seed=7, engine="tracks"):
        started = time.perf_counter()
        if engine not in ("native", "tracks"):
            raise ValueError("engine must be native or tracks")
        if capacity is None:
            if target.graph.get("family") != "zephyr":
                raise ValueError("an explicit capacity is required for other targets")
            g, t = target.graph["rows"], target.graph["tile"]
            capacity = 16*g+1 if engine == "tracks" and g >= 2 and t == 4 else max(1, 2 * (2 * g - 1) * t)
        self.target = target
        self.capacity = int(capacity)
        self.seed = seed
        if self.capacity < 1:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be positive")
        # use_cache=False avoids unrecorded/persistent application cache state.
        # minorminer 0.2.21's uncached g=1 clique routine stalled in this run.
        # Use the explicit interior K_(2t,2t) matching contraction for this case.
        if target.graph.get("family") == "zephyr" and target.graph.get("rows") == 1:
            t = target.graph["tile"]
            if self.capacity > 2*t:
                raise ValueError("g=1 explicit template capacity exceeded; not infeasibility")
            if target.graph.get("labels") != "int":
                raise ValueError("g=1 explicit template requires integer target labels")
            f = dwave_graphs.zephyr_coordinates(1, t=t).zephyr_to_linear
            self.branches = {2*k+j:(f((0,1,k,j,0)), f((1,1,k,j,0)))
                             for k in range(t) for j in range(2) if 2*k+j<self.capacity}
            self.construction = "explicit interior bipartite matching contraction"
        elif engine == "tracks":
            if (target.graph.get("family") != "zephyr" or target.graph.get("tile") != 4
                    or target.graph.get("labels") != "int"):
                raise ValueError("explicit tracks require integer-labeled Zephyr with t=4")
            g = target.graph["rows"]
            if self.capacity > 16*g+1:
                raise ValueError("explicit track capacity exceeded; not an infeasibility certificate")
            # Boothby, King, Raymond (2021), Section 5.1, descriptors A--E.
            descriptors = [[(0,3,0,0)], [(1,3,0,0)]]
            descriptors += [[(0,w,k,1),(1,w,k,1)] for w in range(1,3) for k in range(4)]
            descriptors += [[(0,0,k,j),(1,1+j,k,0)] for k in range(4) for j in range(2)]
            descriptors += [[(0,1+j,k,0),(1,0,k,j)] for k in range(4) for j in range(2)]
            descriptors += [[(0,w,k,j),(1,w,k,j)] for w in range(3,2*g)
                            for k in range(4) for j in range(2) if w+k+j>3]
            assert len(descriptors) == 16*g+1
            f = dwave_graphs.zephyr_coordinates(g,t=4).zephyr_to_linear
            self.branches = {i:tuple(f((*track,z)) for track in descriptor for z in range(g))
                             for i,descriptor in enumerate(descriptors[:self.capacity])}
            self.construction = "explicit Zephyr track descriptors A-E, Boothby et al. Section 5.1"
        else:
            self.branches = {v: tuple(c) for v, c in find_clique_embedding(
                self.capacity, target, seed=seed, use_cache=False).items()}
            self.construction = "minorminer.busclique.find_clique_embedding"
        complete = nx.complete_graph(self.capacity)
        self.validation = verify_embedding(complete, target, self.branches)
        if not self.validation["valid"]:
            raise ValueError("native template construction failed; not an infeasibility certificate")
        self.trees = {v: tree_edges(target, c) for v, c in self.branches.items()}
        owner = {q: v for v, chain in self.branches.items() for q in chain}
        self.contacts = {}
        for q, r in _ordered_target_edges(target):
            if q in owner and r in owner and owner[q] != owner[r]:
                a, b = owner[q], owner[r]
                pair = edge_key(a, b)
                oriented = (q, r) if a < b else (r, q)
                self.contacts.setdefault(pair, oriented)
        assert len(self.contacts) == self.capacity * (self.capacity - 1) // 2
        self.preprocessing_seconds = time.perf_counter() - started

    def embed(self, source, prune=True):
        nodes = sorted(source.nodes)

# Target construction, embedding, and programming notes

This note records the embedding subtask of this autonomous run. It used only the
run prompt, public sources, and artifacts newly written in this run. The target
is an **ideal** Zephyr graph, not an exported device working graph. The installed
generator is `dwave_networkx.zephyr_graph` 0.8.18, the predecessor of the current
`dwave.graphs.zephyr_graph` name. Every saved witness includes all target nodes,
edges, generator version, and parameters. The environment also has minorminer
0.2.21, dwave-system 1.34.0, dimod 0.12.21, networkx 3.5, and Python 3.13.2.

## Explicit polynomial construction

`CliqueTemplate(target, engine="tracks")` is the default. For integer-labeled,
ideal `Z_(g,4)` with `g>=2`, it constructs the published track embedding of
`K_(16g+1)` from Section 5.1 of [Boothby, King, and Raymond, *Zephyr Topology of
D-Wave Quantum Processors*, 2021](https://www.dwavequantum.com/media/2uznec4s/14-1056a-a_zephyr_topology_of_d-wave_quantum_processors.pdf).
A track `(u,w,k,j)` contains every `(u,w,k,j,z)` for `0<=z<g`. The branch
descriptors are implemented literally as A--E in `embedding.py`. Two branches
have length `g`; the other `16g-1` have length `2g`. Thus this complete template
uses exactly `32g^2` qubits, within the target's `32g^2+16g` qubits. This is a
known construction, not a claimed new clique-embedding result.

Here is a direct validity argument for the descriptors. External couplers join
each track. Every vertical interior track (`1<=w<=2g-1`) meets every horizontal
interior track, as follows by choosing the internal-coupler indices in the
published coordinate rule. A peripheral `w=0` track meets the opposite tracks
whose shift is zero. In descriptors B and E each branch has both orientations
of interior tracks. Descriptors C and D have one interior zero-shift track and
one perpendicular peripheral track. The two A branches are the two zero-shift
interior tracks at `w=3,k=0`. These observations give an internal connection
within each two-track branch and a contact for each pair of branches. The
descriptor ranges partition their tracks: B uses interior `w=1,2` with shift
one, C and D use the peripheral tracks and the remaining shift-zero tracks at
`w=1,2`, and E uses `w>=3`, excluding the two A tracks. Thus branch sets are
disjoint. Each constructed template is additionally checked against the exact
generated target graph before use.

For `g=1`, the code explicitly contracts a matching of the interior `K_(8,8)`:
branch `2k+j` contains `(0,1,k,j,0)` and `(1,1,k,j,0)` for `k=0,...,3`,
`j=0,1`. This gives a checked `K_8` using 16 qubits. There is no assertion that
these capacities are maximum minors. Inputs beyond capacity may still fit.

The track construction emits `O(g^2)` qubits. The ideal target has bounded
degree 20 and `O(g^2)` edges. Branch-tree construction, full clique verification,
and extraction of one contact for each logical pair each take `O(g^2)` time and
memory. The implementation traverses integer target labels and sorts only
bounded-degree neighbor lists, so it does not need a global edge sort in this
path. Serialization may separately sort witness lists. These are arithmetic
operation counts; rational bit complexity must be charged separately.

`engine="native"` retains the practical Ocean clique routine
`minorminer.busclique.find_clique_embedding(...,use_cache=False,seed=...)`.
Its default sufficient capacity is `16g-8` and observed branches are shorter.
The explicit path establishes the construction bound; the native path is an
optional measured library baseline. The [Ocean clique documentation](https://docs.dwavequantum.com/en/latest/ocean/api_ref_minorminer/source/clique_embedding.html)
describes native clique search and its caching interface. No persistent cache
was used in the measured native runs.

## Universal restriction and pruning

Once a complete template is checked, every integer-labeled graph with at most
its capacity embeds by assigning variables in sorted order to its first branch
sets. This includes isolated variables. The graph is the actual nonzero
quadratic interaction graph, not the check incidence graph.

Preprocessing fixes a spanning tree for each branch and one contact edge for
every template pair. For a new graph, mark the endpoints of the contact edges
needed by its interactions; remove nonterminal leaves from each branch tree.
An isolated variable keeps one qubit. The remaining tree is the unique minimal
subtree of the chosen tree spanning its terminals. It is nonempty and connected,
contains all required contacts, remains disjoint from other branches, and uses
no more qubits than the original branch. This proves validity and resource
nonincrease relative to this template; it does not compare quantum dynamics.

For `N` source variables, `M` interactions, and `Q<=2gN` selected full-template
qubits, a query costs `O(N log N + Q + M)` time and `O(Q+M)` working/output space.
Its logical ordering can be retained across updates. Repeated syndrome/weight
instances with unchanged graph need no new embedding query. The same reuse is
also available to any previously successful automatic embedding. If H or the
variable graph changes, a fresh query is guaranteed within capacity; a larger
graph requires another declared target/template or a search. A damaged target
must be revalidated and may invalidate the template.

`find_automatic_embedding` calls the general `minorminer.find_embedding`, then
places isolated variables and independently checks the result. Exceeding target
node/edge counts is a certified counting obstruction. An exhausted search,
insufficient leftover isolate space in a found partial embedding, or exceeding
template capacity is **not** a proof that the input has no minor embedding.

## Physical allocation and fidelity

The convention is `x_i=(1+z_i)/2`. The exact Ising conversion preserves constants.
Fields are shared uniformly over a branch; each logical coupler is placed on one
deterministically chosen available contact. Every branch has a BFS tree with
ferromagnetic coupling `-K_i`. Define

`L_i=|h_i|+sum_j |J_ij|`, and choose `K_i=chain_factor*L_i+chain_margin`

with `chain_factor>=1` and positive `chain_margin`. The physical offset is the
logical offset plus the sum of `K_i` over tree edges. Consequently the raw
physical energy of every consistent assignment equals the logical energy.

If a branch is broken, choose one monochromatic component of its tree and flip
the whole component. Every incident tree wall disappears, improving chain energy
by at least `2K_i`. The change of all nonchain terms incident to this component
is at most `2L_i`. Thus some change strictly lowers energy by at least
`2(K_i-L_i)`, and no broken state can be a global ground state. Applying this
argument until consistent proves physical ground-state fidelity. If the exact
logical nonoptimal gap is bounded below by `delta_Q`, the exact raw physical
nonoptimal gap is at least

`min(delta_Q, 2 min_(nonsingleton i)(K_i-L_i))`.

The minimum over no nonsingleton branches is omitted. The argument permits
degenerate optima and does not assume a unique correction.

All fields, logical couplers, reduction penalties, and chain couplers enter a
common positive scale `alpha`. The code supports asymmetric intervals for h and
J and signed sums of coupling strengths in the Zephyr groups generated by
`dwave.system.coupling_groups`. The [official solver-property description](https://docs.dwavequantum.com/en/latest/quantum_research/solver_properties_all.html)
states these are separate constraints. The defaults `h=(-4,4)`, `J=(-1,1)`,
and groups `(-13,10)` are illustrative parameter choices, not claimed properties
of a particular QPU. No device export was available. All alternatives in a
comparison must use the same target and these same chosen intervals. For other
Zephyr tile sizes, callers must supply the correct coupling groups explicitly.

`allocate_physical_exact` builds an exact companion from the compiler's rational
coefficients. The chosen binary64 K values and alpha are treated as exact rational
parameters, and their positive margin is checked against exact logical loads.
Let rho be the sum of absolute errors of all actual programmed h and J values
relative to that companion. If `2 rho < alpha*delta_raw`, every rounded ground
state belongs to the exact ground set. This is the elementary uniform diagonal
energy perturbation bound; it allows selection within a tied optimum. Constant
offset error is recorded but does not affect minimizers. Actual binary64 h/J and
group sums are checked using exact rational arithmetic. If necessary, alpha is
moved toward zero with `nextafter` to make every programmed constraint hold.
Failure of the sufficient fidelity certificate is explicit and means
inconclusive, not proof that the physical minimizers are wrong.

The allocator currently scans the target and groups on every program update:
`O(|E_T|+Q+M)` arithmetic work on ideal Zephyr, with rational error-certificate
work linear in programmed coefficients and group incidences. It does not claim
that these scans are already reduced to the changed weights alone. Contacts,
trees, and group membership could be cached further. This is one limitation of
the implementation's update cost.

## Checks, evidence, and limitations

`results/embed_explicit_tracks_checks.json` verifies explicit complete minors for
g=1,2,3,4,6,8,12. `embed_explicit_tracks_witness.json` contains the entire g=6
target and K97 template. Observed template preprocessing was about 20 ms at g=6
and 96 ms at g=12 in the first run; timings are observations, not asymptotic
proofs. The g=6 complete template has 1152 qubits and maximum branch length 12.

`results/embed_checks.json` records all 1024 graphs on five vertices surviving
template pruning, six kinds of invalid embeddings rejected, 496 QUBO-to-Ising
assignment checks, and physical consistency/ground-state checks on small models.
`embed_physical_witness.json` is an independently inspectable small programmed
model. Additional exact numeric-certificate checks are recorded in the same file.

The separate `embed_benchmark.json` and `embed_target_and_witnesses.json` preserve
the initial nine-graph **native-template** experiment on the same ideal g=4
target, with three seeded automatic reference runs per graph. Graphs include
paths, random cubic graphs, and seeded Erdos-Renyi graphs of 24,40,56 variables.
Native full-template counts were 120,200,280 respectively. Pruned counts ranged
37--246; automatic outputs ranged 24--244. Automatic embedding usually used
fewer physical qubits, while pruned-template queries were faster. Template
queries exclude independent revalidation, whereas the recorded automatic call
includes it; both timing components are given. No claim of overall quality or
annealing superiority follows from these observations. Parent-run matrix
experiments provide the decoding-specific comparison.

Two initial invocations of the uncached native clique routine at g=1 stalled
and later exited with code 137; the precise cause was not diagnosed. This
affected exploratory checks, not saved successful timings. The explicit g=1
construction above avoids that call. The g>=2 native runs completed normally.

Reproduce these checks without credentials:

```sh
python /absolute/path/to/lab/scripts/embedding_checks.py --output /absolute/path/to/lab/results
```

The guarantees concern valid minors, faithful final classical ground states,
explicit programming constraints, finite-precision certification, and
resource/processing costs. Any annealing-path theorem is separate; a smaller
branch count, shorter chain, or larger final-energy scale alone does not prove
better finite-time quantum-annealing success.
class CliqueTemplate:
    """Precompute one checked clique minor and fixed contacts for every pair.

    For a fixed verified target/template, every graph with N <= capacity is
    guaranteed a valid embedding.  Capacity failure says nothing about whether
    a different embedding fits.  With prune=True, keep the unique minimal
    subtree of the fixed branch tree spanning this input graph's contacts.
    """
    def __init__(self, target, capacity=None, seed=7, engine="tracks"):
        started = time.perf_counter()
        if engine not in ("native", "tracks"):
            raise ValueError("engine must be native or tracks")
        if capacity is None:
            if target.graph.get("family") != "zephyr":
                raise ValueError("an explicit capacity is required for other targets")
            g, t = target.graph["rows"], target.graph["tile"]
            capacity = 16*g+1 if engine == "tracks" and g >= 2 and t == 4 else max(1, 2 * (2 * g - 1) * t)
        self.target = target
        self.capacity = int(capacity)
        self.seed = seed
        if self.capacity < 1:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be positive")
        # use_cache=False avoids unrecorded/persistent application cache state.
        # minorminer 0.2.21's uncached g=1 clique routine stalled in this run.
        # Use the explicit interior K_(2t,2t) matching contraction for this case.
        if target.graph.get("family") == "zephyr" and target.graph.get("rows") == 1:
            t = target.graph["tile"]
            if self.capacity > 2*t:
                raise ValueError("g=1 explicit template capacity exceeded; not infeasibility")
            if target.graph.get("labels") != "int":
                raise ValueError("g=1 explicit template requires integer target labels")
            f = dwave_graphs.zephyr_coordinates(1, t=t).zephyr_to_linear
            self.branches = {2*k+j:(f((0,1,k,j,0)), f((1,1,k,j,0)))
                             for k in range(t) for j in range(2) if 2*k+j<self.capacity}
            self.construction = "explicit interior bipartite matching contraction"
        elif engine == "tracks":
            if (target.graph.get("family") != "zephyr" or target.graph.get("tile") != 4
                    or target.graph.get("labels") != "int"):
                raise ValueError("explicit tracks require integer-labeled Zephyr with t=4")
            g = target.graph["rows"]
            if self.capacity > 16*g+1:
                raise ValueError("explicit track capacity exceeded; not an infeasibility certificate")
            # Boothby, King, Raymond (2021), Section 5.1, descriptors A--E.
            descriptors = [[(0,3,0,0)], [(1,3,0,0)]]
            descriptors += [[(0,w,k,1),(1,w,k,1)] for w in range(1,3) for k in range(4)]
            descriptors += [[(0,0,k,j),(1,1+j,k,0)] for k in range(4) for j in range(2)]
            descriptors += [[(0,1+j,k,0),(1,0,k,j)] for k in range(4) for j in range(2)]
            descriptors += [[(0,w,k,j),(1,w,k,j)] for w in range(3,2*g)
                            for k in range(4) for j in range(2) if w+k+j>3]
            assert len(descriptors) == 16*g+1
            f = dwave_graphs.zephyr_coordinates(g,t=4).zephyr_to_linear
            self.branches = {i:tuple(f((*track,z)) for track in descriptor for z in range(g))
                             for i,descriptor in enumerate(descriptors[:self.capacity])}
            self.construction = "explicit Zephyr track descriptors A-E, Boothby et al. Section 5.1"
        else:
            self.branches = {v: tuple(c) for v, c in find_clique_embedding(
                self.capacity, target, seed=seed, use_cache=False).items()}
            self.construction = "minorminer.busclique.find_clique_embedding"
        complete = nx.complete_graph(self.capacity)
        self.validation = verify_embedding(complete, target, self.branches)
        if not self.validation["valid"]:
            raise ValueError("native template construction failed; not an infeasibility certificate")
        self.trees = {v: tree_edges(target, c) for v, c in self.branches.items()}
        owner = {q: v for v, chain in self.branches.items() for q in chain}
        self.contacts = {}
        for q, r in _ordered_target_edges(target):
            if q in owner and r in owner and owner[q] != owner[r]:
                a, b = owner[q], owner[r]
                pair = edge_key(a, b)
                oriented = (q, r) if a < b else (r, q)
                self.contacts.setdefault(pair, oriented)
        assert len(self.contacts) == self.capacity * (self.capacity - 1) // 2
        self.preprocessing_seconds = time.perf_counter() - started

    def embed(self, source, prune=True):
        nodes = sorted(source.nodes)
